lesson.title: Law enforcement
lesson.summary: Separate legally permitted enforcement use cases from the criminal-risk prohibition.

prerequisites.reason: Two listed law-enforcement points expressly depend on the incorporated profiling definition.
The learner must distinguish the listed-use enquiry from the product route.

blocks: **Law enforcement** concerns defined authorities, or activity on their behalf, for prevention, investigation, detection or prosecution of offences, execution of penalties and protection against public-security threats.
A commercial firm using the phrase 'security analytics' does not by that label establish the definition. Record the legally authorised actor, purpose and relationship.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 3(45), 3(46); Annex III 6(a)–(e); Article 5(1)(d)

blocks: Annex III 6 lists permitted enforcement uses: assessing victimisation risk, polygraphs or similar tools, evidence-reliability evaluation, specified offending/re-offending or trait/past-behaviour assessment, and personal profiling in criminal detection, investigation or prosecution.
Keep the five points separate. A victim-risk tool asks a different question from a suspected-offender tool. The lawfulness condition comes before treating the list as permission.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 3(45), 3(46); Annex III 6(a)–(e); Article 5(1)(d)

blocks: Article 5(1)(d) separately prohibits certain individual criminal-risk prediction based solely on profiling or personality assessment. Its factual human-assessment-support boundary is taught in the prohibition module.
An Annex III enforcement listing cannot cure that prohibition. A system may require prohibition analysis before its high-risk duties are even considered.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 3(45), 3(46); Annex III 6(a)–(e); Article 5(1)(d)

blocks: Fictional case: an authorised enforcement body assesses evidence reliability with AI. Record the evidence function under point 6(c), the authority and permitted-use basis, then the remaining classification checks.
Changed case: it predicts offending solely from personal traits. That introduces a separate prohibition question. Keep supporting evidence and unresolved legal permission distinct from vendor claims.

questions.prompt: A supplier calls a product 'security analytics'. What establishes the enforcement context?

options.blocks: Authorised actor, activity and on-behalf relationship
options.reason: The definitions concern legal authority and specified activities.
Branding cannot establish statutory enforcement authority.

options.blocks: Only whether the software is expensive
options.reason: Price does not identify legal authority or purpose.

options.reason: Victim risk is a different function.
